query: Earlier studies of conventional metallic multilayers provide a general framework for deformation, but its conclusions may not transfer directly to high-entropy-alloy systems because compositional complexity, severe lattice distortion, and short-range order are associated with unusual deformation behavior. Preliminary evidence from FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers remains insufficient to establish what controls creep or when a given response dominates. Within the constraints of retaining a nanoscale multilayer coating and balancing strength with deformation tolerance, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading? State what governs the behavior and why, an unspecified controlled comparison that would expose it, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, boundary conditions, relevant prior support, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The steady‐state creep rate in nanoscale FCC/BCC high‐entropy‐alloy multilayer coatings under sustained load is governed by the degree of interface coherence (and associated short‐range order) at FCC/BCC boundaries, because higher coherence/SRO raises the barrier to interface‐mediated dislocation climb and thus slows creep.
generation.material_initial_state: As‐deposited FCC/BCC HEA multilayer (20 nm layers) with semi‐coherent interfaces and minimal annealing, exhibiting short‐range order (SRO) only within layers.
generation.intervention: Post‐deposition anneal at 700 °C for 1 h under inert atmosphere to enhance interface coherence (reduce misfit dislocations) and promote SRO at interfaces.
generation.conditions: T = 600 °C, uniaxial tensile stress = 500 MPa, inert environment, testing time up to 100 h.
generation.structural_mediator: Degree of interface coherence and interfacial short‐range chemical ordering between FCC and BCC layers.
generation.mechanism: Enhanced interface coherence/SRO increases lattice friction and impedes dislocation climb across the interface, forcing dislocations to pile up and slowing the rate of incremental plastic strain under load.
generation.predicted_outcome: The annealed (high‐coherence) multilayer will exhibit a steady‐state creep strain rate approximately 50% lower than the as‐deposited (semi‐coherent) baseline at 600 °C/500 MPa over 100 h.
generation.baseline: Semi‐coherent multilayer exhibits ~1×10^(-5) h^(–1) steady‐state creep rate at 600 °C/500 MPa.
generation.boundary: Valid for layer thicknesses of 5–50 nm, temperatures between 400–700 °C, and stresses 200–800 MPa; outside these ranges, other creep mechanisms (e.g., lattice diffusion creep) may dominate.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate–high; the quantitative effect of SRO on interface diffusion and dislocation climb in HEAs is not fully established.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two identical FCC/BCC HEA multilayers: one as‐deposited (semi‐coherent) and one annealed to enhance coherence. Conduct creep tests at 600 °C/500 MPa for 100 h under identical conditions.
measurements: Creep strain vs. time to extract steady‐state rate
TEM imaging of interface dislocation density and ordering pre- and post-test
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the steady‐state creep rate difference between annealed (high‐coherence) and as‐deposited samples is less than 10%, the hypothesis is falsified.
